newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ford Mexico says workers end work stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Ford Mexico says workers end work stoppage.

text.p: Workers at Ford de Mexico's Cuautitlan plant ended their two-day work stoppage on Wednesday and were heading back to the factory for the second shift on Wednesday afternoon, a Ford spokeswoman said.
Ford de Mexico is a subsidiary of Ford Motor Copany.

"They are now returning to the plant in Cuautitlan (just north of Mexico City)," Ford spokeswoman Guillermina Pilgrim told Reuters. "It could be that work will totally return to normal tomorrow (Thursday)."

Workers at all three Ford plants in Mexico began walking off the job on Friday when the company announced that there would be no profit-sharing for employees because the Mexico unit lost 1.657 billion pesos or about $207 million in 1996.

"Ford, in an act of good will, offered the workers a pre-tax bonus of 3,000 pesos (about $380), and they accepted," Pilgrim said. "It should be clear that this was not profit-sharing because the company made no profits."
Pilgrim said there were 8,000 workers at the three plants.

However, one union member said that only equipment maintenance workers were returning to work and that those on the factory line would hold out until it is determined whether workers would be paid for the time missed due to the stoppage.
"Yes (the union accepted the bonus), but what remains is the issue of the days that work was stopped," Mario Olay of the union's Mexico City office told Reuters. "That will be dealt with tomorrow."
Pilgrim said she had no information about the issue of pay for missing work time.
Workers at the Cuautitlan plant, who began their stoppage on Monday afternoon, stayed off the job even as their comrades went back to work at the two northern Mexico plants.

The Cuautitlan plant makes 468 units a day of the Ford Contour, Mercury Mystique and F-series pickup models for local and export sales, company officials said. Production was stalled for about two full working days.

The Hermosillo assembly plant near the Arizona border halted operations on Friday afternoon and all day Monday before workers returned on Tuesday. The down time cost Ford output of about 1,000 Ford Escort and Mercury Tracer models destined primarily for the United States and Canada, the company said.

At Ford's Chihuahua plant closer to the Texas border, workers walked off the job on Monday afternoon and stayed out on Tuesday, costing Ford output of about 2,000 motors for the domestic and export markets. Chihuahua workers returned to the job on Wednesday.
